thread:
Anya M: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — attaching the staged decomposition plan I sketched in the meeting. High-level: avoid big-bang, extract a thin facade + read-only slice first, validate traffic and metrics, then follow with write path and ownership cutover. Thoughts?

Kevin L: +1 to staged. Can you call out the DB ownership handoff? biggest risk imo is dual-write correctness during transition.

Anya M: Good call. Plan has a synchronous shadow-write phase (write to old service + new service) behind a feature flag, then a delayed verification job that compares a sample of writes. If diff ratio > 0.1% we rollback the flag.

Sarah J: How do we coordinate schema changes? we can't have two services depending on different shapes for long.

Anya M: Schema strategy: backward-compatible column additions only during shadow phase. For breaking changes we use a three-step: add columns, migrate writers, flip readers. We'll gate with a migration_lock table and a low-risk rollout cadence.

Leo P: For traffic routing — suggest start at 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 24h windows with automated health checks. If p50 latency increases >20ms or error rate spike >3x baseline, stop and roll back.

Maria R: What health checks do we want? SLOs are tricky for this path. We should include correctness checks (sampled responses), p50/p95/p99 latency, and token-per-request distribution for inference calls.

Anya M: Agreed. I'll add synthetic correctness probes that run every minute against the canary routing group and a lightweight delta checker. Instrumentation: add tags for "decomp.stage" and "decomp.slice" to traces so we can filter.

Kevin L: Ops question — KV cache ownership for the new service? We can't have two caches fighting.

Anya M: Plan: new service gets a logically namespaced prefix in the shared cache during shadow; reads prefer new prefix when in read-path cutover. At final cutover we migrate prefixes and retire the old keys. We'll include TTLs and a migration window to avoid stale collisions.

Sarah J: Any changes to the runtime batching algorithm needed? different service might have different batching shapes and that affects latency.

Leo P: We'll keep the runtime contract identical for hotpath RPCs. If we need variant batching, it should be a per-instance config behind the same API contract. No behavioral differences expected at the contract layer.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: staging rollout will be orchestrated by the new-decomp pipeline. Triggers: manual start -> canary -> automated progression. See pipeline: https://ci.internal/redwood/pipelines/new-decomp

Maria R: One more risk: cross-team ownership ambiguity. We should have a single owner for the cutover window and a documented runbook for rollback. Suggest Anya + Kevin as cutover leads, Leo as observability lead.

Anya M: Sounds good. Action items: 1) I'll update the RFC with DB migration steps and cache prefix plan (due EOD Fri). 2) Kevin to write the verification job sketch and sample diff queries (due Tue). 3) Leo to add trace tags and synthetic probes to observability backlog (due Wed). 4) Maria to own the runbook doc and contact list.

Kevin L: I'll drop an initial SQL diff query in the RFC thread and sketch the rollout flag toggles.

Sarah J: If anyone runs the shadow job, please include a small dataset example in the PR so reviewers can sanity check.

Anya M: Will do. Thanks all — I'll post the updated RFC link here when done. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: recorded a checklist item for "migration_lock" pattern enforcement in the pipeline.

Leo P: tiny note — let's avoid exploding metrics cardinality with the new trace tags; use a low-cardinality stage tag and keep slice names bounded.

Anya M: Good catch, Leo. I'll normalize slice values to a short enumerated set.

Maria R: Ok locking in leads and dates. If no objections I'll create the follow-up tickets after Anya updates the RFC.

Kevin L: no objections from me.

Sarah J: +1

Anya M: Updated RFC posted: https://rfc.internal/redwood/rfc-2026-staged-decomp — PTAL and I'll create tickets after lunch.

Leo P: LGTM.
